title: Software OpenPGP decompression allocates beyond the configured plaintext limit
root_cause_class: the in-process rPGP provider recursively decompresses an attacker-controlled message and collects the complete literal with as_data_vec before decrypt_authenticated_entity applies max_message_bytes or MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES
demonstrated_impact: A valid 179279-byte received OpenPGP/MIME message expanded to 134217728 plaintext bytes, peaked at 213264 KiB RSS versus an 83664 KiB one-MiB control, and was rejected only after allocation. With RLIMIT_AS=180000 KiB the same message aborted on a 33554432-byte allocation.
impact_tier_reason: A remote sender using only the recipient's public key can select decompressed output large enough to kill the main backend process when a software-key user performs the normal read/decrypt action. The message remains available to retrigger. The OpenPGP feature and user interaction narrow reach but are intended ordinary use, not privileged configuration.
exploit_execution_time_source: Fresh-process decryption time of the retained 128 MiB candidate before the post-allocation size rejection; fixture generation and compilation excluded.
regression_test_or_invariant: Software-provider plaintext is read through a sink capped at min(configured max_message_bytes, MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES)+1, compressed-packet nesting is bounded, over-limit output stops without retaining it, authenticated failure semantics remain fail-closed, and a following ordinary message decrypts successfully.

unintended_behaviors.behavior: the configured plaintext limit is checked only after the complete decompressed literal has been materialized
unintended_behaviors.expected: decompression output is stopped while streaming at the configured plaintext boundary
unintended_behaviors.actual: as_data_vec allocates the entire attacker-selected plaintext before the caller observes its length

composition.unintended_behavior_count_note: A bounded streaming sink in the software provider closes the demonstrated amplification; nesting should be capped in the same decompression-boundary component.
remediation_components: bounded software-provider decompression/output reader with nesting accounting
composition.remediation_component_count_note: The external GnuPG/YubiKey provider already has bounded subprocess output; this component brings the in-process path to the same invariant.
defense_in_depth: run all cryptographic MIME processing in a disposable resource-bounded worker
record compressed-input/decrypted-output ratios for diagnostics without using them as the primary bound
composition.composition_explanation: The post-allocation size check is one misplaced resource boundary.

source_refs.note: provider returns a complete Vec; software path decompresses then calls as_data_vec; size check follows

notes: Specific to OpenPgpSecretKeyProviderKind::Software. GnuPG and YubiKey providers bound subprocess stdout during read.

title: Conversation queues emit attacker-controlled Unicode bidi controls
root_cause_class: draw_queue formats participant and subject strings directly into Ratatui spans while the reader and HTML renderer use explicit bidi/control sanitizers
demonstrated_impact: An ingested subject containing U+202E reached the real Crossterm writer as UTF-8 E2 80 AE (terminal_contains_rlo=true), permitting row reordering on bidi-capable terminals. The reader neutralizes the same character, so the queue is a policy bypass.
impact_tier_reason: The primitive can distort sender/subject/state presentation on bidi-capable terminals but does not mutate trust state or execute terminal commands. Cold mail remains visibly blue and the reader is sanitized; terminals without bidi support do not reorder it.
exploit_execution_time_source: The UI capture itself completes below the retained command's one-second resolution after compilation.
regression_test_or_invariant: Every attacker-controlled queue field passes through one bidi/control sanitizer before width calculation; captured Crossterm output contains none of U+202A-U+202E or U+2066-U+2069 and contains no active C0/OSC sequence.

unintended_behaviors.behavior: the queue bypasses the inert-text sanitizer used by other message presentation paths
unintended_behaviors.expected: attacker-controlled identity and subject text cannot alter terminal bidi state
unintended_behaviors.actual: participant and subject strings are written directly to terminal spans with bidi formatting characters intact

composition.unintended_behavior_count_note: Sanitizing queue fields before truncation closes the demonstrated path.
remediation_components: shared terminal presentation sanitizer for queue participants and subjects
composition.remediation_component_count_note: No parser or trust-model change is required.
defense_in_depth: render visible bidi-control mnemonics instead of silently dropping them
test combining and zero-width format characters across every screen
composition.composition_explanation: One missing presentation call creates the inconsistency.

source_refs.note: queue emits raw strings while the reader sanitizer covers bidi controls
HTML renderer converts bidi controls to visible mnemonics

notes: Direct OSC 52 injection was rejected: Ratatui removed ESC and BEL. This finding is terminal-dependent UI integrity, not arbitrary terminal control execution.

title: IMAP commands permit unbounded aggregate response retention
root_cause_class: async-imap bounds each parsed response but the backend and body-fetch helpers consume server-selected response streams into Vec or other collections without a command-level response-count or retained-byte budget
demonstrated_impact: A real async-imap LOGIN/LIST exchange carrying 40000 valid 34-byte LIST responses sent 1360024 bytes and drove the isolated client to 174004 KiB peak RSS in about 1.03 seconds. Under RLIMIT_AS=150000 KiB the same traffic aborted with SIGABRT on allocator failure.
impact_tier_reason: A configured malicious or compromised TLS-authenticated IMAP endpoint can reliably terminate the main backend during automatic mailbox discovery or synchronization with a small, standards-valid response stream and can retrigger on reconnect. Endpoint control narrows reach but is the explicit threat model of this pass.
exploit_execution_time_source: Fresh release-process time for the retained 40000-response LIST exchange without compilation; the memory-limited variant aborts earlier.
regression_test_or_invariant: Every tagged IMAP command enforces response-count and aggregate-wire-byte budgets before parsed responses escape the stream; backend response size and nesting are lowered; requested UID FETCH consumers reject duplicate target UIDs and cap unsolicited responses; large legitimate flag reconciliation is split into exact 512-UID commands; and an over-budget command returns an error while ordinary Dovecot synchronization remains interoperable.

unintended_behaviors.behavior: only individual IMAP response size and nesting are bounded while a command can retain an unlimited number of individually valid responses
unintended_behaviors.expected: a command-level budget stops response consumption before aggregate retained memory exceeds its configured bound
unintended_behaviors.actual: LIST/FETCH collectors and duplicate-accepting metadata loops grow until tagged completion, timeout or allocator abort

composition.unintended_behavior_count_note: The same absent aggregate command budget appears in mailbox discovery, reconciliation, body-range helpers and header metadata; these are occurrences of one resource invariant rather than independent exploit requirements.
remediation_components: shared budgeted IMAP command-stream consumer with operation-specific item/cardinality and retained-byte ceilings
composition.remediation_component_count_note: Applying one shared budget abstraction to all response consumers closes the demonstrated and sibling paths; wall-clock and individual-response limits remain defense in depth.
defense_in_depth: lower per-response limits on metadata-only IMAP connections
isolate account synchronization in a restartable resource-capped worker
apply account mailbox/message quotas before durable persistence
composition.composition_explanation: One missing aggregate resource boundary is sufficient for process termination.

source_refs.note: LIST and reconciliation FETCH streams are collected before any cardinality policy; SEARCH cardinality is checked after allocation
single-UID body size and range helpers collect every server FETCH response
parsed responses retain backing buffers allocated in 4 KiB blocks
header sync accepts unlimited duplicate matching UID responses before sort/dedup

notes: No code execution or memory corruption was observed. The allocator abort is the demonstrated consequence in safe Rust. The retained 40000-response regression now rejects around 6.7 MiB peak RSS and exits normally under the former 150000 KiB address-space ceiling.

title: Isolated IMAP worker rejects every Landlock-capable Linux host as partially enforced
root_cause_class: enter_landlock applies AccessFs::from_read(ABI::V6) & !Execute, which includes the directory-only ReadDir right, to PathBeneath rules for regular files; landlock 0.4.7 drops the file-incompatible right and records CompatState::Partial, so the ruleset is reported PartiallyEnforced and the worker's own FullyEnforced check fails closed on ordinary hosts
demonstrated_impact: On kernel 6.12.117+deb13-amd64 with Landlock ABI 6, lizard-mail-sync-worker --sandbox-self-test exits 1 with ruleset PartiallyEnforced, and IsolatedImapAccountEngine::sync_once fails with 'IMAP protocol error: isolated IMAP worker protocol failed: early eof' because the worker exits during sandbox setup before answering. The repository guard test cargo test -p lizard-mail-backend --test imap_worker worker_sandbox_is_fail_closed fails at crates/mail-backend/tests/imap_worker.rs:83. In a disposable copy, choosing file-compatible access rights for non-directory paths reports FullyEnforced, keeps all eight self-test denial properties true, and passes the guard test.
impact_tier_reason: The defect is not attacker-triggerable and fails closed, but it disables the isolated receive path on any ordinary Landlock-capable Linux host: synchronization and on-demand content fetch cannot start, and the only configured alternative is the explicitly unsandboxed in-process engine. No memory-safety, authority or data-loss consequence was demonstrated.
exploit_execution_time_source: The worker exits during sandbox setup; the retained guard test reports finished in 0.01 s after build. Build and full-suite compilation time is excluded.
regression_test_or_invariant: crates/mail-backend/tests/imap_worker.rs::worker_sandbox_is_fail_closed requires either a fully enforced ruleset with all eight denial properties or a Landlock-unavailable failure; the reviewed commit produces neither because a capable kernel is misclassified as PartiallyEnforced.

unintended_behaviors.behavior: enter_landlock attaches the directory-only ReadDir access right to regular-file rules such as /etc/hosts and /dev/urandom
unintended_behaviors.expected: A host with Landlock ABI 6 and the standard kernel files should produce a fully enforced ruleset, or file read rules should request only file-compatible rights
unintended_behaviors.actual: landlock 0.4.7 intersects the rule with file-compatible rights, records CompatResult::Partial, and reports the whole ruleset PartiallyEnforced, so the worker always fails closed on ordinary hosts

remediation_components.description: Select access rights per path kind: file-compatible rights (AccessFs::from_file & !Execute & !IoctlDev) for regular files and ReadDir-capable rights only for directories. Verified in a disposable copy: FullyEnforced, all eight self-test denials true, guard test passing.
